content.value: Place one equipment item in the [[article/runic_altar|Runic Altar]]. Your hotbar, inventory, unlocked bags and stored altar tomes supply the carried tome list. The item stays in its equipment slot for repeated crafting.

Transmutation: Normal to Magic with one rune. Augmentation: add a rune to Magic. Regal: Magic to Rare with one rune. Exalted: add a rune to Rare.
Alchemy: reforge editable runes into up to two prefixes and two suffixes; also works on Rare equipment.
Chaos: replace a chosen rune with a weighted random rune on the same affix side.
Annulment: remove a chosen rune. Divine: reroll one chosen rune's numeric values.
Targeted tomes: add the specified family, or select a rune to replace, on Magic or Rare gear. Magic becomes Rare.
Artificial Tome: reserve a rune for the [[article/artificial_tome|Artificial Runic Altar]]. Select a rune to replace if the equipment is full.

For a replacement, removal or value reroll, select the existing rune in the tome details. Scroll this list if necessary. Targeted and artificial tomes also offer Add to free slot when capacity allows. Protected runes cannot be selected.

Roll & compare spends one tome to generate exactly one proposal. Compare the current and proposed rune lists, then choose Keep current or Use new. Both choices consume the paid attempt. The proposal is saved on the equipment, including across closing the screen, moving the item or restarting the server. Resolve it before another rune craft. Browsing a tome or Possible Runes never generates a proposal.

Quality, enchantments, damage, names and unrelated data survive rune crafting. Protected signature runes survive reforging and cannot be replaced or rerolled. Existing fixed Unique items remain locked to tome crafting; their preset properties are unchanged. New and rerolled outcomes obey the equipment cap.

Magic equipment holds one prefix and one suffix; Rare holds three of each. An artificial marker reserves a slot. Possible Runes shows compatible families, sources, allowed tiers and value ranges using the same equipment caps as actual crafting. [[item/minecraft:bow|Bows]] and shields cap at T10, crossbows at T9, diamond at T8 and netherite at T7.
The altar retains its equipment and stored tomes when you close it. You can return to the same equipment for further crafting.
